hints: Look first at the lowest dotted line for pressure in the left atrium. Find the small early bump labelled T, U and V and think about what a small pressure rise and fall means.
Remember that ventricular contraction starts when ventricular pressure shoots sharply upward past atrial pressure, and ends when it falls sharply back below aortic pressure.
walkthrough:
**Spot atrial systole on the atrial pressure line**

Atrial systole is contraction of the atrium, so it causes a small, brief rise in atrial pressure.

On the graph that is the little hill from T up to a peak near U and back down to V. So atrial systole starts at T and ends at V.

**Spot ventricular systole on the ventricular pressure line**

Ventricular systole is contraction of the ventricle, so it causes a huge, steep rise in ventricular pressure.

That steep rise starts at V, just as the atrium finishes. The high pressure is maintained until the ventricle relaxes and pressure crashes down at X, where it meets aortic pressure. So ventricular systole is V to X.

**Use left side timing for the right side**

The left and right sides of the heart beat together. The SAN stimulates both atria together, then after a short delay both ventricles together.

So the times for the right atrium and right ventricle are the same as for the left atrium and left ventricle: atrium T to V, ventricle V to X.

options.A: Correct. Atrial systole is T to V (small atrial pressure wave) and ventricular systole is V to X (sharp ventricular rise to sharp fall). Right side timing matches left side.
options.B: Incorrect. U is the peak of the atrial wave, not the end, and Y is on the low atrial pressure line, not the end of ventricular contraction which is at X.
options.C: Incorrect. Atrial systole starts at T when pressure begins to rise, not at U, and ventricular systole starts at V when pressure first shoots up, not at W when the aortic valve opens.
options.D: Incorrect. V is where atrial systole ends and ventricular systole begins, not where atrial systole starts, and W to Y mixes aortic and atrial points.
